function inflate(strm, flush) {

  var next; /* next input INDEX */
  var put; /* next output INDEX */
  var have, left; /* available input and output */
  var hold; /* bit buffer */
  var bits; /* bits in bit buffer */

  var copy; /* number of stored or match bytes to copy */
  var from; /* where to copy match bytes from */
  var from_source;

  var here_bits, here_op, here_val; // paked "here" denormalized (JS specific)

  output = strm.output;

  input = strm.input;
  have = strm.avail_in;
  hold = state.hold;
  bits = state.bits;

  _out = left;

          bits += 8;

        if ((state.wrap & 2) && hold === 0x8b1f) { /* gzip header */
          state.check = 0 /*crc32(0L, Z_NULL, 0)*/ ;

          hbuf[1] = (hold >>> 8) & 0xff;
          state.check = crc32(state.check, hbuf, 2, 0);

          //=== INITBITS();

          bits = 0;
          //===//
          state.mode = FLAGS;

          (((hold & 0xff) /*BITS(8)*/ << 8) + (hold >> 8)) % 31) {

          state.mode = BAD;
          break;

          strm.msg = 'unknown compression method';
          state.mode = BAD;
          break;
        }

        hold >>>= 4;
        bits -= 4;
        //---//
        len = (hold & 0x0f) /*BITS(4)*/ + 8;

          state.wbits = len;
        } else if (len > state.wbits) {

          state.mode = BAD;

        bits = 0;
        //===//

          bits += 8;

        state.flags = hold;

          strm.msg = 'unknown compression method';
          state.mode = BAD;
          break;
        }

          state.mode = BAD;

          bits += 8;

        bits = 0;

            bits += 8;

            state.head.extra_len = hold;
          }

            //=== CRC2(state.check, hold);
            hbuf[0] = hold & 0xff;
            hbuf[1] = (hold >>> 8) & 0xff;
            state.check = crc32(state.check, hbuf, 2, 0);
            //===//
          }
          //=== INITBITS();
          hold = 0;
          bits = 0;
          //===//
        } else if (state.head) {
          state.head.extra = null /*Z_NULL*/ ;

                state.head.extra,
                input,
                next,
                // extra field is limited to 65536 bytes
                // - no need for additional size check
                copy,
                /*len + copy > state.head.extra_max - len ? state.head.extra_max : copy,*/
                len

              //        len + copy > state.head.extra_max ?
              //        state.head.extra_max - len : copy);

            next += copy;
            state.length -= copy;

        state.mode = NAME;
        /* falls through */

            break inf_leave;
          }

            // TODO: 2 or 1 bytes?
            len = input[next + copy++];
            /* use constant limit because in js we should not preallocate memory */
            if (state.head && len &&
              (state.length < 65536 /*state.head.name_max*/ )) {
              state.head.name += String.fromCharCode(len);
            }

          if (state.flags & 0x0200) {
            state.check = crc32(state.check, input, copy, next);
          }
          have -= copy;
          next += copy;
          if (len) {
            break inf_leave;
          }
        } else if (state.head) {
          state.head.name = null;
        }
        state.length = 0;
        state.mode = COMMENT;
        /* falls through */
      case COMMENT:
        if (state.flags & 0x1000) {
          if (have === 0) {
            break inf_leave;
          }
          copy = 0;
          do {
            len = input[next + copy++];
            /* use constant limit because in js we should not preallocate memory */
            if (state.head && len &&
              (state.length < 65536 /*state.head.comm_max*/ )) {
              state.head.comment += String.fromCharCode(len);
            }

          if (state.flags & 0x0200) {
            state.check = crc32(state.check, input, copy, next);
          }
          have -= copy;
          next += copy;
          if (len) {
            break inf_leave;
          }

          state.head.comment = null;
        }
        state.mode = HCRC;
        /* falls through */
      case HCRC:
        if (state.flags & 0x0200) {
          //=== NEEDBITS(16); */

              break inf_leave;

            have--;
            hold += input[next++] << bits;
            bits += 8;

            strm.msg = 'header crc mismatch';
            state.mode = BAD;
            break;

          bits = 0;
          //===//

          hold += input[next++] << bits;
          bits += 8;

        strm.adler = state.check = zswap32(hold);
        //=== INITBITS();
        hold = 0;
        bits = 0;
        //===//

        /* falls through */

          strm.next_out = put;
          strm.avail_out = left;
          strm.next_in = next;
          strm.avail_in = have;
          state.hold = hold;
          state.bits = bits;

          bits += 8;

        bits -= 2;

        bits -= bits & 7;

          bits += 8;

          state.mode = BAD;

                bits += 8;

                state.mode = BAD;

              //--- DROPBITS(3) ---//

        // state.lencode = state.next;

        //state.distcode.copy(state.codes);

        ret = inflate_table(DISTS, state.lens, state.nlen, state.ndist, state.distcode, 0, state.work, opts);

        // state.next_index = opts.table_index;

        // state.distcode = state.next;

function bitWriter() {
  const bits = [];
  return {
    bits(value, length) {
      for (let i = 0; i < length; i += 1) bits.push((value >> i) & 1);

const path = require('path');
const { pathToFileURL } = require('url');

const ROOT = path.join(__dirname, '../../../../../..');
const COMPILER_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'packages/imba/src/compiler');

let ast;
let compiler;
let STACK;

// The compiler stamps source-map markers like /*%12|3$*/ around generated
// snippets when it runs in tsc mode. They are not interesting for these
// unit tests, so every produced string is normalised before asserting.
const stripMarks = (value) =>
  typeof value === 'string' ? value.replace(/\/\*%[^*]*\*\//g, '') : value;

function compile(source, options = {}) {
  const result = compiler.compile(source, {
    sourcePath: '/virtual/test.imba',
    ...options,
  });
  const errors = (result.diagnostics || []).filter(
    (diagnostic) => diagnostic.severity === 1,
  );
  if (errors.length) {
    throw new Error('Unexpected compile errors: ' + JSON.stringify(errors));
  }
  return result;
}

function classOf(result) {
  const cls = result.ast
    .body()
    ._nodes.find((node) => node instanceof ast.ClassDeclaration);
  if (!cls) throw new Error('No class declaration was parsed');
  return cls;
}

function fieldsOf(cls) {
  return cls.body()._nodes.filter((node) => node instanceof ast.ClassField);
}

function fieldNamed(cls, name) {
  const field = fieldsOf(cls).find((node) => String(node._name) === name);
  if (!field) throw new Error('No field named ' + name);
  return field;
}

// ClassField#c() reads the "current" node from the compiler STACK to decide
// whether it is compiled as part of a class body, an instance-init block or a
// static-init block. The surrounding stack is faked here so each branch can be
// exercised in isolation.
function withStack(nodes, callback) {
  const previous = STACK._nodes;
  STACK._nodes = nodes.slice();
  try {
    return callback();
  } finally {
    STACK._nodes = previous;
  }
}

function renderField(field, nodes) {
  return stripMarks(withStack(nodes, () => field.c()));
}

beforeAll(async () => {
  ast = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(COMPILER_DIR, 'nodes.mjs')).href);
  compiler = await import(
    pathToFileURL(path.join(COMPILER_DIR, 'index.mjs')).href
  );
  STACK = ast.STACK;
});

afterEach(() => {
  STACK._nodes = [];
});

describe('ClassField#c() early exits', () => {
  test('returns undefined for struct fields, before any other work is done', () => {
    const result = compile('class A\n\tstatic s = 2');
    const cls = classOf(result);
    const field = fieldNamed(cls, 's');

    // Sanity check: without the struct option the static initializer is emitted.
    expect(
      renderField(field, [result.ast, cls, cls._staticInits]),
    ).toBe('this.s = 2;\n');

    field.set({ struct: true });
    expect(renderField(field, [result.ast, cls, cls._staticInits])).toBe(
      undefined,
    );
  });

  test('returns undefined when the field is excluded by an inactive env flag', () => {
    const result = compile('class A\n\t$web$ x = 1\n\t$node$ y = 2', {
      platform: 'node',
    });
    const cls = classOf(result);
    const webField = fieldNamed(cls, 'x');
    const nodeField = fieldNamed(cls, 'y');

    expect(webField.isExcluded()).toBeTruthy();
    expect(nodeField.isExcluded()).toBeFalsy();

    expect(renderField(webField, [result.ast, cls, cls._inits])).toBe(
      undefined,
    );
    expect(renderField(nodeField, [result.ast, cls, cls._inits])).toBe(
      'this.y = ($$ && ($0 = $$.y) !== undefined) ? ($0) : 2;\n',
    );
  });

  test('compiles the field when the matching env flag is active', () => {
    const result = compile('class A\n\t$web$ x = 1', { platform: 'web' });
    const cls = classOf(result);
    const field = fieldNamed(cls, 'x');

packages/imba/changelog.md:7:* Fix name resolution inside `yield` expressions. The compiler marked the method as a generator but did not traverse the yielded value, so nothing in that value was resolved. An implicit-self call such as `yield helper(1)` compiled without `this.` and threw `ReferenceError: helper is not defined`, also when the call was an argument (`yield self.finish(build(u))`) or inside a closure. The same gap left amperfunctions untransformed (`yield items.map(&.name)` referenced an undefined `v$`), did not make a method with `await` inside `yield` async (a syntax error), read the wrong variable when a redeclared `let` was renamed, and crashed the compiler on a tag literal. A call inside `yield` to a module-level `def` that is declared after the class now compiles to `this.name()`, as the same call does outside `yield` — declare such a `def` above the class.
packages/imba/changelog.md:26:* Memoize amperfunctions that close over local variables. Previously only capture-free amperfuncs (hoisted to shared module-level functions) and self-referencing ones (memoized per instance) kept a stable identity — an amperfunc capturing a local like `items.find(&.id == x)` compiled to a plain closure recreated on every call. Such functions are now memoized per combination of `self` and the captured values, so the same values yield the same function identity across calls and renders. Object captures are held weakly, so memoization does not retain them.
packages/imba/changelog.md:28:    This only applies when every captured variable is effectively final. If a captured variable is reassigned anywhere in its scope (including `++`, compound assignment, and destructuring assignment), the amperfunc stays a plain closure and the compiler emits a warning pointing at the capture. Capture analysis is also more thorough — captures hiding in index access (`&.list[idx]`), string interpolation, and ternaries are now found and handled correctly.

describe('Access#js - numeric members', () => {
  test('brackets a numeric member', () => {
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Num('2'))).toBe('user[2]');
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Num('0'))).toBe('user[0]');
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Num('10_000'))).toBe('user[10000]');
  });

  test('unwraps an index node around a number', () => {
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Index(new Num('2')))).toBe(
      'user[2]',
    );
  });

  test('unwraps an index node around a string', () => {
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Index(new Str('"name"')))).toBe(
      'user.name',
    );
  });

  test('unwraps an index node around a symbol', () => {
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Index(new SymbolNode(':name')))).toBe(
      'user.name',
    );
  });

  test('compiles a negative index through the negIndex helper', () => {
    expect(dot(new Num('2'), new Num('-1'))).toBe('negIndex$__(2,-1)');
    expect(dot(new Str("'items'"), new Index(new Num('-3')))).toBe(
      "negIndex$__('items',-3)",
    );
  });
});

describe('Access#js - safe chaining', () => {
  test('reports safechain only for the ?. operator', () => {
    expect(new Access('.', new Identifier('a'), new Identifier('b')).safechain()).toBe(false);
    expect(new Access('?.', new Identifier('a'), new Identifier('b')).safechain()).toBe(true);
  });

  test('prefixes dot accesses with ?. for safe chains', () => {
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Identifier('name'), '?.')).toBe(
      'user?.name',
    );
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Str("'name'"), '?.')).toBe(
      'user?.name',
    );
  });

  test('prefixes bracket accesses with ?. for safe chains', () => {
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), new Num('2'), '?.')).toBe('user?.[2]');
    expect(dot(new Identifier('user'), 'expr', '?.')).toBe('user?.[expr]');
  });

  test('uses the optional negIndex helper for safe negative indexes', () => {
    expect(dot(new Num('2'), new Num('-1'), '?.')).toBe('optNegIndex$__(2,-1)');
  });
});

describe('Access#js - left hand side handling', () => {
  test('falls back to the scope context when there is no left side', () => {
    expect(dot(null, new Identifier('name'))).toBe('globalThis.name');
  });

  test('compiles self as the scope context', () => {
    expect(dot(new Self(), new Identifier('x'))).toBe('globalThis.x');
  });

  test('parenthesizes a number used as the context of a dot access', () => {
    expect(dot(new Num('2'), new Identifier('b'))).toBe('(2).b');
  });

  test('keeps a string context as is', () => {
    expect(dot(new Str("'abc'"), new Identifier('length'))).toBe(
      "'abc'.length",
    );
  });

  test('remembers the starting location of the left or right operand', () => {
    const left = new Num('2');
    left._startLoc = 4;
    const access = new Access('.', left, new Identifier('b'));
    generate(access);
    expect(access._startLoc).toBe(4);
  });

  test('keeps an explicit starting location', () => {
    const left = new Num('2');
    left._startLoc = 4;
    const access = new Access('.', left, new Identifier('b'));
    access._startLoc = 42;
    generate(access);
    expect(access._startLoc).toBe(42);
  });
});

describe('Access#js - implicit access', () => {

});

  TOKENIZE: 1,

  PARSE: 4,

};

export class CompilationResult {}

export class Compilation {
  static current;

  static error(opts) {
    return this.current?.addDiagnostic?.("error", opts);
  }

  static warn(opts) {
    return this.current?.addDiagnostic?.("warning", opts);
  }

  static info(opts) {
    return this.current?.addDiagnostic?.("info", opts);
  }

  static deserialize(data, o = {}) {
    let item = new Compilation("", o);
    return item.deserialize(data);
  }

  constructor(code, options) {
    this.sourceCode = code;
    this.sourcePath = options.sourcePath;
    this.options = options;
    this.flags = 0;
    this.js = "";
    this.css = "";
    this.result = {};
    this.diagnostics = [];
    this.tokens = null;
    this.ast = null;
  }

  step(flag) {
    if ((this.flags & flag) == flag) {
      return false;
    }
    this.flags |= flag;
    return true;
  }

  deserialize(input) {
    let val;
    try {
      val = JSON.parse(input);
    } catch (e) {
      console.log("failed", input, this.options);
      throw e;
    }
    this.rawResult = val;
    this.deserialized = val;
    return this;
  }

  serialize() {
    if (this.rawResult) {
      return JSON.stringify(this.rawResult, null, 2);
    }
  }

  tokenize() {
    if (this.step(STEPS.TOKENIZE)) {
      try {
        Compilation.current = this;
        this.lexer.reset();
        this.tokens = this.lexer.tokenize(this.sourceCode, this.options, this);
        this.tokens = this.rewriter.rewrite(this.tokens, this.options, this);
      } catch (e) {}
    }
    return this.tokens;
  }

  parse() {
    this.tokenize();
    if (this.step(STEPS.PARSE)) {
      if (!this.errored) {
        Compilation.current = this;
        try {
          this.ast = this.parser.parse(this.tokens, this);
        } catch (e) {}
      }
    }
    return this;
  }

  compile() {
    this.parse();
    if (this.step(STEPS.COMPILE)) {
      if (!this.errored) {
        Compilation.current = this;
        try {
          this.result = this.ast.compile(this.options, this);
        } catch (e) {
          // internal compiler error - report it as a located diagnostic so it
          // flows through the same channel as parse errors instead of crashing
          let loc = e._loc;
          if (!(loc && loc[0] >= 0 && loc[1] >= loc[0])) {
            loc = [0, 0];
          }
          let orig = e.error || e;
          this.addDiagnostic("error", {
            message: "Internal compiler error: " + (orig.message || orig),
            source: "imba-compiler",
            range: this.rangeAt(loc[0], loc[1]),
          });
          console.error(
            "[imba] internal compiler error in " + (this.sourcePath || "<unknown>") + "\n" +
              (orig.stack || orig),
          );
        }
      }
      if (this.options.raiseErrors) {
        this.raiseErrors();
      }
    }
    return this;
  }

  recompile(o = {}) {
    if (this.deserialized) {
      let js = this.deserialized.js;

      return res;
    }

    return { js: this.js };
  }

 * Unit tests for TagAttr#js(o) in packages/imba/src/compiler/nodes.mjs
 *
 * TagAttr#js delegates to a number of compile-time branches depending on the
 * attribute name, namespace, owning tag (SVG / form controls) and the current
 * compilation platform.  The helpers below compile a tiny Imba fixture to put
 * the compiler's internal STACK into the right state, then call the target
 * method directly on the produced TagAttr node.  This keeps the assertions
 * focused on the string returned by TagAttr#js itself.
 *
 * In addition, a few tests inspect the final compiled program to cover the
 * tsc platform (which emits source-map markers when js() is called directly)
 * and the observable STACK side effects of the method.
 */

const path = require('path');
const { pathToFileURL } = require('url');

const COMPILER_PATH = path.resolve(
  __dirname,
  '../../../../../../packages/imba/src/compiler/compiler.mjs',
);
const NODES_PATH = path.resolve(
  __dirname,
  '../../../../../../packages/imba/src/compiler/nodes.mjs',
);

let compile;
let TagAttr;

beforeAll(async () => {
  const compilerModule = await import(pathToFileURL(COMPILER_PATH).href);
  compile = compilerModule.compile;

  const nodesModule = await import(pathToFileURL(NODES_PATH).href);
  TagAttr = nodesModule.TagAttr;
});

/**
 * Compile a small Imba snippet and fail the test if the compiler reported any
 * diagnostic (parse errors would otherwise silently produce empty output).
 */
function compileFixture(source, platform) {
  const out = compile(source, {
    platform,
    format: 'esm',
    sourcePath: '/tmp/tag-attr-fixture.imba',
    config: {},
  });

  const diagnostics = out.diagnostics || [];
  if (diagnostics.length) {
    throw new Error(
      `Unexpected compiler diagnostics for ${JSON.stringify(source)} (${platform}): ` +
        diagnostics.map((d) => d.message).join('; '),
    );
  }

  return out;
}

function firstTag(out) {
  const nodes = (out.ast && out.ast.body && out.ast.body()._nodes) || [];
  const tag = nodes.find((node) => node && Array.isArray(node._attributes));
  if (!tag) {
    throw new Error('Fixture did not produce a tag with attributes');
  }
  return tag;
}

// Unit tests for TagContent#js() in packages/imba/src/compiler/nodes.mjs.
//
// TagContent#js() lowers a single tag child into JavaScript source. The method
// delegates the final rendering of the wrapped value (`value.c`), variable
// naming, symbol lookup, and DOM calls to collaborators. Those collaborators
// require a fully traversed compiler stack, so here they are replaced with
// deterministic stubs while the branching logic under test remains untouched.

let N;

const NODES_PATH = "../../../../../../packages/imba/src/compiler/nodes.mjs";

beforeAll(async () => {
  N = await import(NODES_PATH);
});

let savedTsc;
let savedPlatform;

beforeEach(() => {
  savedTsc = N.STACK._options.tsc;
  savedPlatform = N.STACK._options.platform;
});

afterEach(() => {
  if (savedTsc === undefined) {
    delete N.STACK._options.tsc;
  } else {
    N.STACK._options.tsc = savedTsc;
  }
  if (savedPlatform === undefined) {
    delete N.STACK._options.platform;
  } else {
    N.STACK._options.platform = savedPlatform;
  }
});

function onlyChildFlags() {
  return N.F.TAG_FIRST_CHILD | N.F.TAG_LAST_CHILD;
}

/** A non-special TagLike parent that is neither a Tag nor a switch fragment. */
function makePlainParent(cvar = "PC") {
  const parent = new N.TagFragment({});
  parent.cvar = jest.fn(() => cvar);
  return parent;
}

function makeTagParent(opts = {}) {
  const parent = new N.Tag({});
  if (opts.slot) parent._kind = "slot";
  parent.cvar = jest.fn(() => opts.cvar || "PC");
  return parent;
}

function makeSwitchParent(cvar = "PC") {
  const parent = new N.TagSwitchFragment({});
  parent.cvar = jest.fn(() => cvar);
  return parent;
}

/**
 * Build a TagContent whose compiler collaborators are deterministic.
 * The real `value()`/`isStatic()`/`isDetached()`/`isOnlyChild()` logic is
 * kept because it participates in the branches under test.
 */
function makeContent(value, opts = {}) {
  const content = new N.TagContent({
    value,
    detached: !!opts.detached,
  });

  content._parent = opts.parent || makePlainParent(opts.cvar);
  content._flags = opts.flags === undefined ? 0 : opts.flags;
  if (opts.tvar !== undefined) content._tvar = opts.tvar;
  content._o = opts.o;

  content.runtime = () => ({ renderContext: "CTX" });
  content.domCall = (name) => "[dom:" + name + "]";
  content.osym = (ns = "") => "sym" + ns;
  content.bvar = () => "BB";
  content.ref = () => "RR";
  content.vvar = () => "VV";
  content.key = () => "KK";
  content.fragment = () => ({ tvar: () => "FF" });

  return content;
}

function str(value = '"hi"') {
  return new N.Str(value);
}

function num(value = 7) {
  return new N.Num(value);
}

function text(content = "TEXT") {
  const node = new N.TagTextContent("x");
  node.c = jest.fn(() => content);
  return node;
}

function call(content = "CALLEE()") {
  const node = new N.Call();
  node.c = jest.fn(() => content);
  return node;
}

function bangCall(content = "BANG()") {
  const node = new N.BangCall();
  node.c = jest.fn(() => content);
  return node;
}

function plain(content = "VAL") {
  return { c: jest.fn(() => content) };
}

For `.foo` with {scope} where scope has cssid and cssns: addScopeClass(part, cssns()), then scope undefined, so cssid not used. Hmm. `scope.cssid` used only in scoped pseudo and scope injection. For `* .foo` with scope: outer isScope injected, then for each part isScoped && scope: add ns to inner; then scope && o.scope: id = o.id || cssid? -> addScopeClass(scope,id). Let's test.

Need test scope injection `o.id` adds scope object with id class.

Also `o.ns` with localpart logic. Let's test.

const path = require('path');

const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../../../../..');

let rewrite;
let selparser;

  ]);
  rewrite = selparseModule.rewrite;
  selparser = parserModule;
});

function parse(selector) {
  return selparser.parse(selector);
}

function run(selector, options = {}) {
  return rewrite(parse(selector), null, options);
}

function collectParts(ruleSet) {
  const parts = [];
  let part = ruleSet.rule;
  while (part) {
    parts.push(part);
    part = part.rule;
  }
  return parts;
}

function lastPart(ruleSet) {
  return collectParts(ruleSet).at(-1);
}
